historical_reviews.deepseek: ForceRestart is relevant only after firmware mapping and target validation; the proposed observation cannot prove an immediate reset or safe recovery.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly distinguishes the forced-reset oracle from the preceding orderly reboot and retains explicit approval, quiescence and recovery.
historical_reviews.history: No earlier record exists for this exact code/variant.
historical_reviews.v3_1: The test must preserve evidence of an unclean reset rather than demanding graceful shutdown semantics; the critical acceptance is one forced transition followed by a new, healthy boot without a reset loop.

original_test_intent: Exercise the BMC Immediate Reboot control as an abrupt host reset and verify that the selected SUT performs one forced reboot and returns to an acceptable operating state.
original_method: Verify the target and advertised Immediate/ForceRestart mapping, stop all workloads and writes, capture boot/filesystem/log baselines, select Immediate in the BMC Web control and issue exactly one reboot, observe the forced transition with bounded console/BMC polling, then prove a new boot identity, expected services and filesystem health while retaining abrupt-reset evidence.
manual_activity: The owner approves the abrupt-reset window and exact BMC action after confirming storage/workload quiescence; an operator watches the independent console path, performs recovery if needed and owns the verdict.
required_inputs: BMC Web Immediate semantics and supported ForceRestart mapping
Proof active writes, storage operations and workloads are stopped
Pre-reset boot ID and filesystem/service baseline
Independent BMC/console recovery and reset-loop escape plan
safety_requirements: Never force-reset during active writes, firmware update or critical workload
Use one verified target and protected validated BMC session
Do not call the operation orderly or expect graceful shutdown evidence
Do not use a fixed sleep as transition proof
Never automatically retry after rejection or timeout
Stop on wrong action, BMC loss, boot failure, filesystem error or reset loop
Preserve kernel/journal/SEL evidence and do not clear logs
agent_execution_scope: Collect target, boot and storage/workload baseline
Operate the literal Web Immediate control or explicitly accepted equivalent once
Capture bounded reset and return timeline
Collect new boot identity, filesystem/service and abrupt-reset evidence
Report facts without assigning PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED
engineer_actions: Approve the target, Immediate/ForceRestart mapping and maintenance window
Confirm no active writes or workloads
Define transition, boot and filesystem acceptance

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: ForceRestart can represent Immediate Reboot only when advertised and owner-approved; one `PowerState` read after five seconds cannot prove the forced transition, new boot or filesystem health, and the risk wording is semantically wrong.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the BMC Web Immediate action or approved ForceRestart equivalent once, with console/BMC timeline, changed boot ID and explicit filesystem/service recovery checks.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Immediate mode, one reboot and 10/20-minute estimates are retained; no graceful semantics or repeat resets are introduced.

modernized_recommendation.status: SINGLE APPROVED FORCED RESET WITH DATA-INTEGRITY RECOVERY ORACLE
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Correlate the action acknowledgement with console discontinuity, BMC reset event, reachability loss/return, changed boot ID, filesystem checks and service readiness; preserve any unclean-shutdown records as expected diagnostic evidence.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Defines immediate-reset evidence and recovery gates while keeping the source's abrupt BMC action.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: An API ForceRestart may cover the underlying operation only by explicit equivalence; it does not inherently cover the source's BMC Web UI selection. Final PowerState alone does not prove a reboot.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Even after quiescence, a forced reset can corrupt firmware-managed caches or expose latent filesystem/boot faults, so one-shot execution and console recovery are mandatory.

project_override_considerations: The Project must approve whether Redfish ForceRestart is equivalent to the Web Immediate option and define the expected abrupt-reset indicators. The preceding Orderly Reboot and following Orderly Shutdown must retain their distinct graceful oracles.
expected_evidence: Verified SUT/BMC identity, advertised action mapping, approval and quiescence proof
Pre-reset boot ID, workload/storage/filesystem/service state and timestamps
Single BMC Web Immediate action or approved equivalent request/response
Forced reset timeline from BMC/console/reachability evidence
Changed boot ID, expected uptime, filesystem health, mounted storage and service readiness
Journal/dmesg/syslog/SEL forced-reset evidence, recovery actions, no-secret audit and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently specify an immediate reboot. The DeepSeek reference to orderly operation is rejected as a review-layer error, not a source contradiction.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The exact action mapping, window, quiescence, acceptance and recovery are normal execution inputs; the immediate forced-reset purpose is clear.

review_improvement: Makes abruptness an explicit part of the oracle, corrects the historical orderly wording and replaces a final-state sample with a complete forced-reset and recovery timeline.
independent_technical_reasoning: Immediate reboot intentionally bypasses graceful OS shutdown, so success cannot be evaluated by orderly-shutdown evidence. It requires proof that exactly one forced transition occurred and that the resulting boot and filesystems are usable. A final `On` state is compatible with no reboot at all, making boot identity and reset-event correlation essential.
